utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-69-PT, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good day, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, we have Marek Michon as a new TA on the case. Case manager, Janet Stewart, and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, Mr. Geert-Jan Knoops for the accused, Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, my name is Zoran Jovanovic, attorney from Belgrade, and I represent the Defence of Mr. Simatovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I read from the website of ICTY that this should mark the first proceedings in this institution so I would like to take this opportunity to wish you all a very happy new year. Since the last Status Conference dated 29th of September last year, there have been certain though not much developments in the case. First, a joinder motion was denied on 10th of November. Was it appealed, Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we did not appeal it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Prosecution's second amendment of the indictment of this case it was allowed by the Chamber decision on 16th of December and the Prosecution filed its amended indictment on 20th of December and there have been a request from the Defence for certification for appeal on 21st. And yesterday, the Trial Chamber issued its decision on the variance of protective measures as the Chamber sees the Milosevic case. I understand the Defence should have received them. I see them nodding. And there are some -- a couple of pending motions. One is a temporary modification of the provisional release conditions for the Accused Stanisic, and we are waiting for the government's assurances. And then the request from the Defence for certification for appeal against the decision of an amendment of the indictment is being considered by the Chamber, and the Chamber will make its decision in due course.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, in relation to this issue I would like to mention something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: You may have noticed that the Prosecution did not respond to this motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Actually, at the time, first of all, almost nobody was there, everybody was on vacation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But, of course, there was here a person in charge and correctly this person felt that there was no need to respond to this motion because all the argument that is we had given that actually supported the decision had been given in the previous filings so there was no need. The only two things I would like to mention because Mr. Jovanovic raised it in his motion for certification, we still don't have the Stoparic statement that was given to the Belgrade district court investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is C-063.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes and we have requested it and we will receive -- we were assured that we will receive it very soon but we still do not have it. And in relation to Mr. Knoops' submission we don't have the full transcript of the Skorpion video. It's in the pipeline and as soon as we have it we will disclose it. That's what I wanted -- want to mention in relation to the certification. I mean, I reject the allegations that we did violate our disclosure obligation. We can only disclose what we have in hand and in our possession, and therefore we did disclose what we have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. That should have been noted by the parties and also, it will be noted by the Chamber as well. And if the Trial Chamber rejects -- only if it rejects the Defence motion for certification or later Appeals Chamber confirms the amendment of the indictment, there will be needed a further appearance pursuant to the Rules. So in that case, would the Accused be able to come to The Hague? Are you in the position to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, my humble submission is that in the event -- in the unfortunate event the certification would not be granted or when granted the Appeals Chamber would not allow the appeal our preference is this the initial appearance for the accused Mr. Stanisic could be conducted by means of a videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It should be further appearance not initial appearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, further appearance. You're correct, Your Honour, thank you. This is our submission. Also in light of his current medical condition, I was myself from the 28th until the 30th in Belgrade. I've spoken with his medical team and his situation has aggravated since the submissions we made to the Honourable Trial Chamber several months ago. In this light, we anticipate the filing of a motion on the fitness to stand trial earlier than expected. As Your Honour may know, we have filed a motion in which we have notified the Chamber and the Prosecution on the current medical situation of Mr. Stanisic substantiated with a detailed medical report. During my interviews with his medical team over Christmas, it turned out that the situation again has aggravated and, if the Chamber wishes, we -- sorry, we can file an updated verse on the medical status in due course. But in light of his current medical condition and also in view of the practical its of a potential return to The Hague for a further appearance, we humbly submit that it could be considered to have this further appearance being conducted through a videolink and we are familiar with the practice of this Court that it has been conducted before in a case, in the Plavsic case where the guilty plea of the accused was conducted through a videolink. So this is the standpoint the Defence in the case of Mr. Stanisic for the event that the further appearance should be conducted in due course after the decisions your Honourable Trial Chamber is going to make on the certification, presuppose the certification would be denied or the Appeals Chamber would eventually deny the appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it from your submission that there would be no problem for the Accused to appear for the purpose of the further appearance through video or telephone link.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The Accused is able physically and mentally to attend a further appearance through the videolink as proposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jovanovic, can I hear from you on this point. You take the same position?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, absolutely the same position. I think that it would be far more practical and less costly and let me just also mention that quite recently a videolink was established between the district court in Belgrade, the department for war crimes, with the Court in Sarajevo so I think that all the technical conditions set in place and I think it would be superfluous now to change the decision on provisional release although it would be necessary if the Accused were to be returned to The Hague and then to Belgrade. So the accused Franko Simatovic is in good health but I think it would be far better if that were to be done on the basis of videolink or some such link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. Can I ask Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff whether the Prosecution has any opposition to having a further appearance through videolink?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution, of course, would prefer to have the Accused both here to attend the further initial appearance and -- but if such an application is being made for videolink in particular for Mr. Stanisic for health reasons, nothing can be done against this but I would rather like to see such an application in particular then also a confirmation by a doctor confirming that he's not able to travel because that's the point, whether he's able to travel to The Hague or not. And not so much that he is in bad health. I mean that's for sure but whether he's able to travel or not. If such an application is made and such a documentation is provided we would, of course, not object against it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that means that you're objecting to having a further appearance in case of Mr. Simatovic, not even for the sake of judicial economy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: If Mr. Stanisic is not able to travel here, then I would rather say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it Mr. Simatovic is very healthy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: He is able to travel, yes, so I think he should be here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that when necessary, the Chamber will consider the matter but I would encourage the Defence to file their motion if they wish to have the further appearance to be conducted through video or telephone link. And I think I exhausted the points I noted down so I would like to ask the parties if there is any further issues to raise at this moment. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From the Defence? Yes, Mr. Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I assume that you have asked the Defence to give a written submission about an appearance of the Accused so we are going to wait for your decision and then we will put in our demand for a videolink, of course, if your decision is such and ruling is such that it rejects the Defence's request to appeal. The second thing that I would like to say is that if the Chamber rejects the certification submission by the Defence, there is a deadline for launching a request and this was on second amended indictment and the date was the 20th of December, and this means the 20th of January. We received an additional statement by C-063 Witness, on the 12th of January pursuant to Rule 66. I don't know if that is additional supportive material so in the case -- in case you should reject the Defence's request we would like to know when the deadline for an appeal of the decision is set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jovanovic. The Defence of Mr. Stanisic are requested for that kind of somewhat sort of stay in their motion so I don't think there is any reason to treat differently. So that will be considered by the Chamber in its decision on the request for certification for appeal. So the both -- speaking for myself, both the Accused will be treated in the same manner. If that pleases you. Is there any more -- any points, Mr. Knoops?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether my learned friend has finished his submissions in this regard but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have one more point to raise but it is quite a different matter. The Prosecutor informed the Defence or rather the OTP informed the Defence that Milan Martic's trial has gone ahead and that during that trial evidence will be presented which will -- some of which will be exculpatory pursuant to Rule 68 with respect to Stanisic and Simatovic. The OTP said that it would be disclosing to the Defence those materials which are to be presented in private closed sessions and that the Defence should pay attention to the evidence that will be tendered during the public open sessions. I think that this once again in a way is pushing the ball into our court pursuant to Rule 68 and I don't think it is practical for the Defence to follow a trial that might last for even a year, up to a year, and to wait to see whether some material will crop up which comes under Rule 68 with respect to the Accused Stanisic and Simatovic. If the OTP is ready to go ahead with Martic's trial, and I'm sure it stands trial ready, in view of the fact that it is continuing on the 17th of January I think that the Prosecution at this point in time knows which material could come under Rule 68 already now and thus disclose to the Defence in the trial of Stanisic and Simatovic and the Defence will certainly take an active part and follow the proceedings because it is relevant for its trial too. But I think that at this point in time the OTP could be in a position to inform the Defence about the list of witnesses, list of exhibits, which could be disclosed to the Stanisic and Simatovic Defence pursuant to Rule 68. So other wise, we would have to wait for months perhaps and follow the trial for months before any material crops up or before we ourselves find something that might be exculpatory and come under Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I followed you in full. What the Prosecution said to the Defence, as I understand it, is that a possible exculpatory material evidence may be led in Martic case so the Prosecution asked the Defence of Mr. Simatovic and Stanisic to pay attention of the public part of the proceedings. Am I right in so understanding? Can I hear from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I think I can actually clarify something for Mr. Jovanovic. Mr. Jovanovic at the moment we have no idea what will be Rule 68 in the Martic trial because the Rule 68 material will come from the Defence in the Martic case and we don't know what they will present in their cross-examinations or later in the Defence case. So what we have so far exculpatory materials related to Martic that you have already got because the cases are related. What we will do is, of course, when the Martic trial is running, each witness that is also a witness in your case here, you will get the transcripts according to Rule 66(A). You get them complete because that's our obligation under Rule 66. But under Rule 68 because it's a public trial we do not provide you with those public sources, but what we do, we provide you with Rule 68 materials that come in in private or closed session because you don't have access to it. And that's what we will review for you and provide to you, but in relation to the public sources it's your own responsibility and we have alerted you that there may be something coming up. Whether it does, we don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it clarifies the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right. All I didn't understand was that the OTP meant the Defence material in Martic's trial. I thought it was material relating to Rule 68 in the Martic trial which might possibly be exculpatory with regard to the accused Stanisic and Simatovic. So if they know what material they have in their disposal then I had expected that to be disclosed, but of course I will actively follow the proceedings as I do all other proceedings relevant to our trial as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: In this sense I would support the submissions of my learned colleague that it's our view that if the interpretation of the letter of the Prosecution of the 11 January 2006 is as such that it has fulfilled or will fulfill its obligations under Rule 66 and/or 68 by means of putting the Defence on notice for the Martic trial, even the public sessions thereof, we believe and I think this is also the argument of Mr. Jovanovic that this is not fulfilling the obligations under the Rules as such. You cannot simply say to the Defence in every case, you can follow the trial yourself and find out what is 66 and/or 68. So I, on behalf of the Defence of Mr. Stanisic, would like to stress that although we are appreciative of the letter of the Prosecution and that we are put on notice that the trial will take place and will potentially result in exculpatory evidence, we still believe that the Prosecution has not fulfilled its obligations by merely putting Defence on notice to fulfil the obligations under Rule 66 or 68. That is the point the Defence would like to make. Beforehand I think the Prosecution is able to provide for instance the Defence in the Stanisic case and the Simatovic case with an overview of, for instance, the exhibits and their witnesses under Rule 66 they are seeking to admit in court, and our point is that we as Defence, we can timely anticipate the filing of these documents in our case instead of waiting until the trial will progress for months and perhaps a year and we are simply then too late in our pre-trial preparations based on the documents which will emerge from the Martic trial, and I think this is the right moment to stress this position of the Defence in the case of Mr. Stanisic that we don't believe that the Rules should be interpreted in that sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. What I understand from the Prosecution submission is somewhat different. What the Prosecution had already in their possession should have been disclosed either in 66(A)(i) or (A)(ii) or 68. What they have -- what the Prosecution had in mind is that the new evidence emerging from Martic case, from the Defence case, will be disclosed and if it is a public document and they will not provide for -- specifically for that. I think that's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and that is the usual practice here. The Prosecution does not disclose under Rule 68 the public open source material. That's -- but we have informed you that there may be something upcoming, and whatever a witness says who is also a witness in your case, that, of course, you will receive as Rule 66(A) material. But I don't see any obligation that we have to provide you with the -- give you an outline of the Martic case. I mean, you can have this -- everything is in public hearings and you have the witness list in the Martic case. That's all public documents that you can easily get from the Internet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. It might be a bit too early to raise this but by the amendment a crime base has been added and all the disclosure has been done or not, only the supporting material has been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, only the supporting material so far but there isn't actually much else to disclose as far as I see. There isn't really that much added. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I assume that pre-trial brief should be amended or newly filed, and anything you will make a comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. What we are actually at the moment doing is preparing the final pre-trial brief, dropping the crime bases that were dropped and adding the Srebrenica part and we also will provide the final witness and exhibits list. It will take I've discussed it with my colleague who is actually doing it and as the Stanisic and Simatovic trial team is a small one, we think we will have it in two months, if that's acceptable for anyone. We would file it in two months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that is only after the certification is rejected or the Appeals Chamber confirms the Trial Chamber's decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Actually I can say we will file -- of course, if it is not granted we don't need to file anything new, but if it is granted it's still the two months from now. So let's say in month there is a decision, a further month and we file, so it's not that we start doing the work in -- starting only after the decision. We are actually in the process putting it together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the scale of the case or length of the trial, number of witnesses can be dealt with at the next Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but I can say it will not be more than now because we are dropping something and we are adding something so it will basically be the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Some witnesses should be changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any other points to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise if I've been going on and on, but quite simply we did not have a 65 ter meeting before this Status Conference so we could not present some of our arguments. Related to C-063 and the statement of that witness that my colleague stated just now, that this was not received although it was taken by the investigating judge from the Belgrade court for war crimes, I think it's a rather important statement. I simply cannot believe that after so many months, that I told the OTP that this statement exists, and at the Status Conference the OTP said that practically the Defence assisted them in disclosing relevant materials, discovering relevant materials. I think this is a very important statement, and I also presented that in the request for certification of appeal too. So again, if the Defence's request is rejected, I still think it is very important for this statement to be attached to the second amended indictment. How should I put this? It's strange that there are these ongoing comments about the good cooperation, intense and very good cooperation between the war crimes department in Belgrade and the OTP and both offices of the Prosecutor have said that. It's quite unbelievable that they haven't managed to receive this one statement in months. The Defence, we work in cooperation after all, we asked the commission for cooperation with the ICTY to get this statement but I told the OTP that the statement is where it is so I would kindly ask my learned friends to insist on it. If that is not sufficient material for the actual request for certification of appeal, could it please be taken into account when they make their preliminary objections to the amended indictment? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is -- something is important for the Defence, it is as important to the Prosecution as well. So I think Prosecution will be doing its best to get the material, and just note for that -- I'm speaking for myself, whether there is a prima facie case or not is not a matter to be considered in -- in the motion for this -- for the request of certification for appeal. But that's -- having said that, I think there is no further issues. Mr. Knoops, do you have anything to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, sorry. In the absence of a 65 ter Conference, I beg your indulgence for three points I would like to raise. One has to do -- the first two points have to do with disclosure and one issue with the filing of a potential motion. Your Honour, the Defence has noticed that the B/C/S versions of the expert reports in the Milosevic case, from Mrs. Borrelli, Neilsen, and Tunents [phoen], apparently are not on the JDB, and we -- our legal assistant went with the Registry searching through these JDB and we were not able to find the B/C/S versions of the three expert reports in the Milosevic case. So perhaps the Prosecution is able to verify whether this is indeed correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you identify the items again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One of them is Mr. Tunents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Tunents? Expert report of Mr. Tunents, the expert report of Mr. Neilson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Nielsen?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: The expert report of Mr. Borrelli. We have the English versions but not yet the B/C/S versions and we were not able to identify them on the JDB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say those were from the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes, from the Milosevic case, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't remember the last two, Neilsen and Borrelli.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That can be checked by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think Neilsen, I'm not really sure that it's from the Milosevic case but I'm sure he testified in the Krajisnik case so -- but I can't be sure. But I think he only testified in Krajisnik case and Borrelli, Borrelli I'm also not sure whether that's Milosevic or Krajisnik, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That may be the reason why the Defence was not able to find it JDB but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But we will also now see where to locate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Prosecution will pay attention to that and then second thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: The question whether the Prosecution is able to disclose if that's the case any additional reports or documents filed by the national council regarding the activities of the Serbian DB. Some months ago we have filed a list with search terms to the Prosecution I think prior to one of the Rule 65 ter Conferences and we were not able to detect any documents filed from the national council on the Serbian DB and one of our main questions is whether the Prosecution is in the possession of such documents and, if so, whether these documents could be disclosed and these relate specifically to the activities of the Serbian DB in 1991, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow what the national council is regarding the activities of the Serbian DB. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, do you follow that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I actually don't know what body that should be. In relation to the search terms we have already before the Status Conference today Your Honour we have discussed that we need to meet and discuss certain issues, the Defence and Prosecution, and one of the issues that we actually need to discuss, and my colleague who is in charge of disclosure has alerted me to this, the Defence provided us with a list of search terms but it's basically a list of issues and it's very difficult to search what you want to us search. In the way you formulated, it's not possible. If you ask for certain issues, you can't use the search term -- the issue is a search term and then we find it all now. We will have to discuss how we can find the things that you would like to have to certain issues and that's a point that we need to discuss. As far as I know, what we have on the Serbian DB was disclosed, I mean, when it was a Rule 68 was disclosed, and we have to continue further searches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would like to indicate to the parties and in particular to the Defence that Status Conferences is not the only time to communicate with the parties so I would like to encourage to you communicate with the Prosecution to find that's -- an appropriate way much disclosure. Can I ask the what is the last point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm grateful for the answer of the Prosecution, thank you. Last point, Your Honour, is just an information for Your Honours and the Prosecution that already indicated in my first submission this -- during the Status Conference that the Defence is anticipating the filing of a motion on the fitness to stand trial of the Accused Mr. Stanisic far earlier than indicated in our motion which was dealt with by the Trial Chamber, our last motion on this issue, Your Honour, based on the latest medical information. As Your Honours may remember, and also the Prosecution, we have indicated in that earlier motion the intention to file a concrete release from the Chamber once the trial schedule would be at stake. Yet it is our belief now, as matters stand now, to pursue with filing of such a motion earlier and I hope Your Honours that we can inform the Chamber in due course when this filing will be made, in which filing we will request the Chamber for a hearing of three or four medical experts on this issue and I endeavour to file that motion in February, if time allows me, and the reports are received by then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider whenever it is filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Of course, but I thought it would be appropriate to inform Your Honours about the intention of the Defence because it will mean a slight deviation from the announcement made in the earlier motion in this regard. Thank you very much for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, for your information. The Chamber will be on alert but you will bear in mind that the points ordered by the previous Chamber's decision that a specific condition of the Accused may be a -- confidential but whether he's ill so as not to stand fit to the trial, is it -- I think it's a public matter. There should be a good cause if it is to be in -- it is to be dealt with in confidential way. Anything else? I noted no -- none. The hearing is now adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
